**UNO – Quick‑Start Rules** | Section | What you need | |---------|---------------| | **Deck** | Standard UNO set (108 cards):
• 90 numbered cards (0–9) in four colors (Red, Green, Blue, Yellow).
• 8 “Skip”, 8 “Reverse” and 8 “Draw Two” cards.
• 4 “Wild” and 4 “Wild Draw Four”. | | **Goal** | Be the first player to score at least 500 points over one or more rounds. Points come from the cards left in opponents’ hands when someone goes out. | --- ### 1️⃣ Setup 1. Shuffle the full deck thoroughly. 2. Deal each player 7 cards face down; keep them secret. 3. Place the remaining deck facedown as the *draw pile*. Flip its top card onto the discard pile—this starts the play. *If the flipped card is an action card (e.g., Skip), apply it immediately before anyone plays.* --- ### 2️⃣ Turn Order & Direction - Players sit around the table clockwise. - A **“Reverse”** card flips direction instantly (clockwise ↔ counter‑clockwise). - In two‑player games, Reverse acts like a normal card (no effect). --- ### 3️⃣ Playing Cards On your turn you may: | Card Type | How It Works | |-----------|--------------| | **Numbered** | Must match either color OR rank with the top discard. Example: if Red 5 is on top, you can play any red card or any 5. | | **Action** (`+2`, `Skip`, `Reverse`) | Same matching rule applies. After playing:
- `+2`: Next player draws two cards and loses their turn.
- `Skip`: Next player simply misses their turn.
- `Reverse`: Change direction; next player becomes whoever was previously behind you. | | **Wild** | Can be played regardless of color/rank. You declare the new active color. | | **Wild +4** | Same as Wild but forces the next player to draw four cards unless they challenge (see below). | #### If you have no playable card: - Draw one card from the draw pile. - If that drawn card is playable, you may use it right away; otherwise end your turn. --- ### 4️⃣ Special Rules | Rule | Explanation | |------|-------------| | **Drawing Until Playable** | Some house variations allow drawing repeatedly until you find something you can play. Officially only one card per turn. | | **Calling “UNO!”** | When you’re reduced to exactly one card, shout “UNO!”. Failure to do so before another player takes their turn results in a penalty: you must pick up two extra cards. | | **Challenge (“Wild +4”)** | Opponent suspects you had a legal non‑wild card instead of using Wild +4. They call “challenge.” Both players reveal hidden cards:
• If you did indeed have a playable card, you must take six cards total (four from the wild plus two penalty).
• If not, you pay the penalty yourself. | | **Stacking (+2 / +4)** | Many groups permit stacking: if Player B plays a +2, Player C may respond with another +2 (or +4 if allowed); the next player then has to draw cumulative cards unless they stack again. This isn’t part of official rules but common in casual play. | | **End of Round** | Once a player discards all his/her cards, round ends. Score points based on opponent’s hand values: numbers count as face value, Action/​Wild cards add 20, Wild +4 adds 50. Add those totals to the winner’s score. Start a new round with fresh shuffling. | --- ### 5️⃣ Winning the Game Play continues through multiple rounds until a player's accumulated score reaches **at least 500 points**. That player wins! *(Some families shorten this threshold to 200 or even 100 for quicker sessions.)* --- ### Handy Tips - Keep track of which colors dominate the board; holding many of the same color gives flexibility later. - Save your Wilds for moments where you’ll likely run out of matches. - Pay attention to the last few cards others hold—you might anticipate who will win soon. Enjoy! 🎉
